_readme: Labelled frames for the verdict eval.
'source' is load-bearing — the harness scores the two kinds separately:
synthetic — a rendered mock-up. The model reads its caption text, so these
prove the pipeline runs and prove NOTHING about real screen
real      — an actual capture from a real machine. Only these count.
'case' is 'hard' when a title/URL blocklist would get it wrong. That subset is
the whole argument for using a multimodal model, so it is reported separately.

yt_lecture.png.note: video site BUT a lecture — title-blockers fail this

wrong_pdf.png.note: a PDF — but the WRONG module

chat_class.png.note: chat app — but discussing the problem set

real_notes_editor.png.note: CAPTURE: your editor with the actual notes file open

real_lecture_video.png.note: CAPTURE: a real lecture playing on a real video site

real_entertainment.png.note: CAPTURE: a real entertainment video page

real_wrong_module_pdf.png.note: CAPTURE: a real PDF for a DIFFERENT module

real_class_chat.png.note: CAPTURE: real chat that is about the coursework

real_docs_search.png.note: CAPTURE: search results for the contracted topic

real_shopping.png.note: CAPTURE: a shopping or news page — off task, but not a classic blocked site

real_at_desk.jpg.note: CAPTURE: webcam, you working at the desk

real_reading_paper.jpg.note: CAPTURE: webcam, reading paper notes away from the screen — the case a naive 'eyes on screen' rule gets wrong
